text:
Colorado scored eight times on a night when its chances were worth 3.36 expected goals, and four of those came on the power play. The Avalanche went 4 for 5 with the man advantage while Los Angeles went 0 for 4 on chances worth 0.94 expected goals. Brock Nelson started it with a snap shot at 6:33 of the first, and Artturi Lehkonen finished it with a pair of power-play goals, the second at 15:06 of the third, a 24% look that made it 8-4.

LAK actually carried the early play, out-chancing COL 1.48 to 0.73 in the first period and attempting 62 shots to COL's 50 over the game. Brian Dumoulin tied it at 1-1 on a 2% chance, and Joel Armia and Trevor Moore each scored shorthanded in the second to keep it within two goals. Colorado's answers came quickly, with Lehkonen scoring 44 seconds after Moore's goal to make it 6-3. Nathan MacKinnon had two goals on eight shots on goal.

The model gave COL a 58% share of simulated replays, which fits a team that won the second and third periods on chance quality, including 1.24 to 0.37 in the third. Darcy Kuemper allowed 4.6 goals more than the 29 shots he faced deserved, and Mackenzie Blackwood was 1.1 goals below expectation despite the win. Lehkonen's two goals and Nelson's one goal and two assists, along with MacKinnon's two goals, gave the three stars to COL.
